<description>
**Problem:** `gettxoutsetinfo`, `scantxoutset`, and `dumptxoutset` retain LevelDB iterators after releasing `cs_main`.
While those iterators are live, AssumeUTXO cache rebalancing can call `ResizeCache()`, replace `m_db`, and cause LevelDB to abort.
The issue was [reported during review of #35465](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35465#discussion_r3428902672).

**Fix:** Each cursor holds a shared lock on `m_db_mutex` for its lifetime.
Compaction takes the same shared lock, allowing it to run alongside cursors.
`ResizeCache()` takes the lock exclusively and waits for both before replacing `m_db`.
Checked shared-lock wrappers and non-LIFO lock tracking preserve Core's locking diagnostics, including for the existing signature-cache and parallel cuckoo-cache users migrated in this series.

**Risk:** `ResizeCache()` holds `cs_main` while it waits, so a long-running UTXO scan can stall validation, message processing, and RPCs that need that lock during cache rebalancing.
Current callers destroy cursors on the thread that created them. A cursor holder must not acquire `cs_main` unless it already holds it.

This is a concrete example of the lifetime interactions created by rebalancing the snapshot and background chainstates, as discussed in [#35054](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35054#issuecomment-4488453829).
The fix protects the current lifecycle and can be reviewed independently of the discussion about making snapshot trust explicit and simplifying background validation in [#32377](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32377).
</description>
